cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's Audit Machine check user access at HANGS Construction Services.
First it matches every user account in four systems to the staff list from HR.
Two people who left can still sign in.
Segregation of duties means no one person can both start and approve a payment.
One person approved about $65,000 of their own payments.
Next it lists every administrator account and compares the sign-in settings with the policy.
Then it traces every system change to its approval. One had none.
Now it rates each weakness by what it could let through.
Then it writes the workpapers and a draft findings memo for the CPA.

All done. It proposes one material weakness, a gap that could let a large error through: the controller's unchecked administrator rights. It also proposes one significant deficiency, payments approved by the person who made them. Ten items stay open. The CPA, a person, decides and signs. The machine gives no opinion.
